claim: Johnson, Gillespie and Vance report prospective observations of triage interruptions at two adult EDs in 2015. Eight triage nurses were followed for 118 triage-interview observations; 67 were classified as interrupted. Table 1 uses N=67 for interruption categories. Its separate Source > Self and Cause > Self rows each report 7 (10.5%); these are separate marginal dimensions, and their equal counts do not establish case-level overlap. The Results prose describes self-interruptions as remembering something previously intended or getting misplaced supplies, without separating those examples. The paper does not report a supply-specific retrieval count, equipment/supply class, distinct retrieval trigger, origin or destination, trip-purpose taxonomy, search/travel/work duration, item availability, or reusable origin-destination matrix. These trip-specific fields remain unknown; this source supports qualitative structural evidence only and supplies no generic parameter, rate, distribution, heuristic, or model default.

primary_source.revision: Johnson KD, Gillespie GL, Vance K. Effects of Interruptions on Triage Process in Emergency Department: A Prospective, Observational Study. Journal of Nursing Care Quality. 2019;33(4):375-381. Text-mining BioC JSON snapshot for PMCID PMC6037611, retrieved from NCBI PMC BioC API; exact local source bytes bound by SHA-256.

location.paragraph: BioC passage offsets 4492 (study design), 4841 (two ED settings), 5123 (nurse sample), 8676 (118 observations), 10237 (self-interruption examples), and Table T1 at offset 21361.

primary_source.population: Eight participating triage nurses at two adult emergency departments in one health system: an urban Level 1 trauma center with 55 ED beds and a suburban Level 3 trauma center with 28 ED beds. The study reports 118 observed triage interviews, of which 67 were interrupted; Table 1 interruption categories use N=67. Convenience sample; vulnerable-population triage encounters were excluded.
primary_source.period: Prospective observations over six months in 2015; observations were conducted between 7 am and 7 pm.
primary_source.units: Counts and percentages of the 67 interrupted triage-interview observations for Table 1 categories. The 10.5% value is the table's percentage for all self-classified interruptions, not supply-retrieval trips. No supply-trip units or durations are reported.
primary_source.licence_access: NCBI PMC BioC text-mining snapshot; manuscript metadata and notice state it is available for text mining and may be used consistently with fair use. No general open-republication licence is asserted.

transformation.description: Read the exact packet-bound BioC JSON snapshot. Extracted study design, setting/sample and observation counts from the Methods/Results passages, the combined self-interruption description from Results, and the two Self rows with denominator N=67 from Table T1. Kept the table's combined self-interruption category distinct from the prose examples of remembering a prior task and retrieving misplaced supplies. No supply-trip count, rate, purpose class, O/D data, duration, availability, distribution or model value was derived.
transformation.input_units: BioC JSON text; triage-interview observation counts; Table 1 counts and percentages.
transformation.output_units: Qualitative source claim with study scope and table denominator; no supply-trip measurement or simulation parameter.

report_lineage.section: Task choice, continuity and interruptions; supply/equipment paragraph

review.notes: Independent source readback passed. The two Table 1 Self values are separate margins and do not establish case-level overlap; neither is a supply-trip count. Accepted only as bounded qualitative evidence and an explicit trip-data gap; no empirical model use or transferable default.

independent_readback.reason: Independent direct retrieval matched the exact 52,268-byte BioC JSON snapshot hash. Methods, Results, Table 1 and R5 line 55 reproduce the sample, separate category margins, grouped self-interruption examples and lack of supply-specific trip measurement.

locator_evidence.locator_checked: Methods BioC offsets 4492, 4841 and 5123; Results 8676, 9444 and 10237; Table 1 T1 offset 21361; R5 line 55

transformation_evidence.method: Independently fetched the NCBI PMC BioC endpoint, recomputed SHA-256, located the stated Methods/Results passages and Table 1 rows, and compared the record and R5 lineage.
transformation_evidence.comparison: Source confirms 118 observations and 67 interrupted observations; Table 1 separately reports Source Self 7 (10.5%) and Cause Self 7 (10.5%) under N=67. Results groups remembering prior intended work with getting misplaced supplies. It reports no supply-specific count or trip attributes. The equal marginal counts are not treated as overlapping cases or supply trips.
